Lets say for the sake of a thought experiment that I'm an angry troll and I want to attack you personally for some reason. Maybe I perceive you as bad at the game, or maybe I think you insulted me in some way. The actual reason might be completely unknown to you. I may not even have a reason. For some, it's a mini-game to see how over the edge they can push you.

The first thing I'm going to do is consider the information available to me, which is almost nothing. I'm going to try to put you on the defensive and keep you there as long as possible. From a defensive posture you're more likely to reveal details about yourself that I can use against you. I know you're female, I know you play games. I'll attack one of those things. Gender is an easy target for a troll regardless of sex because most of us can't possibly conform to the ideal standard of attractiveness and success. If you're a woman I'll try to insinuate you're less than the ideal woman. If you're a man, I'll try to insinuate you're less than the ideal man.

For example, I might say "oh, well, you're fat, ugly, and so desperate you'll sleep with anyone" - since this paints a picture that you're far less than the standard of what society sees as the ideal woman, the response most people will come back with will be defensive. If they are in a relationship, they may divulge that. If they have a family they may let that slip too. If they have no problem frequently getting sexual partners, that can also come out.

Just a side rant here to break it up: Frankly saying you're having too much sex is the most laughable thing in my opinion. I mean, how many people on their death beds - male or female - do you think say "my only regret is that I wish I hadn't had so much sex?". I wish we as a culture would get over seeing sex as evil. Anyway, back on track.

Allowing a troll to manipulate you is an error, because every piece of information you give them is ammunition. Once they discover they can learn about you by insulting you, they'll keep playing off the answers you give them in an attempt to find the holy grail - a piece of information that is both insulting, and true by your own admission. Or even better, a piece of information that you've given that is a lie, and is proven a lie by your own admission. If you're caught in a lie they can directly attack the credibility of anything you say from that point on. If there's an audience, they'll attempt to get the audience on their side. In their mind, the more people agreeing with them, the more correct they are.

It's the same for a guy. They might attack my job, my income, my sexual orientation, my attractiveness, etc. Anything that is important to the average man. The gender is different, but the objective remains the same.

I don't think a lot of women are making up stories. I think it's entirely likely that at some point they were attacked like this in some way. Following the laws of averages, if one person has been attacked in a given way there are likely others who have had similar experiences. The difference here is that guys are taught from birth not to show weakness. So it's far less likely that a guy will come forward to tell his abuse story. In abuse cases, women become the vocal minority by virtue of the fact that society deems it acceptable for a woman to be emotionally vulnerable to abuse.

Some feminists really do have their heart in the right place, and genuinely want to stop abuse because they believe it to be a problem endemic to something they love. The common mistake is that they fail to gather sufficient information to build a strong case, or they fail to consider other root causes of the behavior. Are you in a team game and performing poorly? Are you playing so well you're making them look bad with your performance? Are you talking a lot over the mic about irrelevant things? Are you making a lot of jokes people aren't finding funny? Each situation may have its own mitigating factors, but rarely are single instances of abuse ever examined closely enough to determine how or why they go down. Examining the causes or triggers can give us clues about what can be done to combat the problem.

Other feminists are blatantly taking advantage of the first group. They're the opportunists. They go out of their way to build a case because they intend on making a career out of it. In my opinion, these people are worse than the trolls because they tend to instill ideas that simply aren't true in those who would listen. They tend to blow problems out of proportion in order to suit an agenda - the proverbial "CNN terrorism effect". If you tell people that the terrorists are among us for long enough, people will start looking for terrorists everywhere. Muslim? Terrorist. Dark skin? Terrorist. Spend significant time in the middle east? Well, you get the idea. The psychology of people and their fears has been extensively studied, and the sad truth is that we are very easy creatures to manipulate. Successful career feminists use this knowledge to their advantage.

People making careers on the foundation of these arguments are participating in the worst kind of exploitation because it instills a sense that any women who plays games is a victim. That if you're a woman considering playing games you'll be a victim. That no matter what they do they'll always play second fiddle. It creates people who stop trying to better themselves, because now they can pass the blame instead of actively trying to improve.

Anyway, In answer to your ultimate question, "is it bullshit?" the answer is that it's not easy to answer that question. Abuse can't all be lumped in to the same category, because it doesn't all have the same root cause. There are definitely people out there who are stupid enough to think that because you're a woman that you're incapable. Let them think that if they want, especially if you're playing competitively against them. It will lead to them seriously underestimating you.
